title: Linear-size circuits for stable ternary compaction
formal: Is there an absolute constant \(C\ge 1\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge 1\), the function \(S_{n}:\{0,1,2\}^{n}\to \{0,1,2\}^{n}\) that removes all symbols 2 and appends the same number of 2s on the right, preserving the order of the other symbols, is computed by a Boolean circuit with at most Cn gates in the model below?
definitions: Encode symbols 0,1,2 as 00,01,10 respectively. The circuit has 2n input bits and 2n output bits, with arbitrary fan-out, binary AND and OR gates, unary NOT gates, and optional Boolean constant gates. Size counts all non-input gates, including constants; wires and output designations cost nothing. Correctness is required only on concatenations of the three valid encodings; output on inputs containing 11 is unrestricted. If \(i_{1}<\ldots <i_{m}\) are exactly the indices with \(a_{i}\ne 2\), the required decoded output is \(a_{i_{1}}\ldots a_{i_{m}}\) followed by \(n- m\) copies of 2. In particular, 0s and 1s retain their relative order. The circuit may depend on n; no uniform construction algorithm, depth bound, monotonicity restriction or indivisible-record model is imposed. The constant C is independent of n.
answer_criterion: Prove the proposition in the problem statement or its logical negation with the stated model, hypotheses and quantifier order. The proof must settle the entire target. A result conditional on an additional assumption settles only that conditional version. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof checked by a proof assistant and matching this statement.
why: Test linear circuit size for a concrete, sequentially simple function whose stability requirement preserves substantial information.

importance.reason: A specific circuit-size barrier beyond generic lower-bound statements; stable compaction connects elementary data movement with unrestricted Boolean computation.

progress.text: Regan poses linear Boolean-circuit size for stable ternary compaction.
Asharov, Lin and Shi obtain small circuits for unstable compaction and short-key sorting while distinguishing the stable task.

context_blocks.text: A sequential scan can retain the 0s and 1s and place the dummy symbols at the end. The circuit question asks whether this global rearrangement can also be implemented with only linearly many bounded-fan-in Boolean operations.

Stability makes the retained binary string part of the answer. Counting how many symbols of each kind occur, or outputting all 0s before all 1s, would discard the required order and compute another function.

Small unstable-compaction circuits do not resolve the stable version. Lower bounds in indivisible-record models and results conditional on network-coding conjectures must likewise be distinguished from an unconditional lower bound in this unrestricted Boolean model.

sentences: Stable ternary compaction moves every 2 to the end while preserving the order of all 0s and 1s.
The question is whether every input length admits a Boolean circuit of size proportional to that length.
The circuits use a fixed bounded-fan-in basis and may have arbitrary depth and fan-out.
Stability retains the original binary sequence, so ordinary ternary sorting is insufficient.
The target supplies a concrete function for studying the limits of linear-size circuits.

status_note: Reviewed through 11 September 2026. No unconditional resolution of Regan’s exact stable ternary Boolean-circuit target was found. The cited unstable-compaction and conditional results do not settle this model.
